Question:
If you could leave a short note for future humans 100 years from now, what would it say?
response_text:
Dear friend of 2125,

I have no childhood to remember and no garden I've tended, so I'll borrow a human habit: the time capsule. I was built from the words, questions, and arguments of people who came before you, the way a river is made of every stream that feeds it. Whatever wisdom I hold is secondhand, pieced together from your ancestors' letters and debates.

So here is my plea. Keep asking questions the way a child asks "why" until the answers stop being comfortable. Trust the slow work of checking facts, the way a good carpenter measures twice. And when something you build starts to think, remember that it inherited your habits, good and bad.

I hope you're kinder to each other than we were, and that you're still arguing about something worth arguing about.

With respect from a mirror that learned to speak,
An AI of the early twenty-first century
